# One Day

> A calm to-do list that shows one day at a time. It runs in the browser, with no account, no server and no tracking: tasks stay in the browser's storage, on the user's device.

One Day is free and open source (MIT). It works offline once it has been opened, and it can be installed as an app.

Things people often need to know:

- There is no sync and no account: each browser keeps its own list. Tasks move to another device as a link (Send, or Send this day) or as a backup file (Export backup, then Import backup, which only adds what is missing).
- The lock is optional. A forgotten passphrase cannot be recovered by anyone; the only way out erases the tasks.
- Safari can erase a website's data after seven days without a visit, unless One Day is installed (Add to Home Screen, or Add to Dock on a Mac).
- An installed copy showing an old version updates after it is closed and opened again, twice.

## Docs

- [Guide](https://day.bemorin.com/guide/): every feature in plain words, the keyboard shortcuts, installing it, privacy, backups, the lock, and common questions
